unlisted_practices: Enact a federal statutory preemption provision, limited to AI applications used in health care, that bars states from imposing product safety and efficacy requirements different from or in addition to federal requirements.
Leave regulation of the use of AI tools in clinical practice to the states.
Create voluntary, fit-for-purpose FDA pathways for integrated devices and pure autonomous software.
Review integrated devices in two stages: individual component review, then comprehensive review of the integrated device's performance.

Oversee pure autonomous software through a total product lifecycle approach, with post-market surveillance the responsibility of the developer in partnership with hospitals and clinicians as appropriate.
Maintain the FDA's existing 510(k) and PMA pathways and the predetermined change control framework within its risk-based regulatory framework.
Hire additional software engineering and AI talent at the FDA, using the Title 21 pay authority.
Base federal AI oversight on the FDA's least burdensome principles.
Build pragmatic regulatory safe harbors, akin to those in the 21st Century Cures Act, to promote incremental innovation.
Establish clear post-market surveillance frameworks for health care AI.

screen.reason: This is a legal and policy commentary/perspective proposing a federal preemption clause and modernized FDA oversight framework for AI-enabled medical devices, drawing historical lessons from the 1976 Medical Device Amendments.
